chapter: Jump for Joy and the Harlem clubs
title: Jump for Joy gets fixed in Los Angeles
summary: The Ellington show 'Jump for Joy' broke in Los Angeles, Nick Castle choreographed, and a movie actor Bigard cannot name fixed the slow parts so houses packed; backers pulled out, Duke was too scared to carry it himself, and it closed despite good tunes.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Tell me about Jump for Joy.
Oh, 'Jump for Joy' was a terrific show. I mean, they had some great guys that, you know, -- it broke in here in Los Angeles -- and the guys like some movie stars came over to straighten the show out.
Who?
One of the guys that died recently. He always played bad guys in the movies. I should -- He limps a bit, quite a bit. A short guy.
MS. BIGARD
I think Nick Castle was the choreographer.
Yeah, Nick Castle was the choreographer.
But this guy -- gee, some parts of the show was kind of slow and they couldn't get that part straight for nothing till this guy came in. When he came in he straightened that whole show out.
think of it, [John Garfield]
Well, when you (Inaudible.)
Huh, I wonder who it was.
He died. He's dead. I'll probably think about it as I go along.
He didn't get any credit in the program.
No. He didn't want any credit.

Well, anyway, the show was supposed to go to San Francisco and then to Chicago and then to New York. But at first the show wasn't taking on so good and the guys that had the money invested, in it they was scared, and after this guy had fixed it -- the show -- you couldn't get in the show then. Every night it was packed and jammed. And during that time the guys had pulled all their money out and Duke was trying to get new backers because everybody was crazy about the show, even the people that saw it.
He couldn't get the backing so they had to close the show, but it was a fantastic show.
I know it had a lot of talent in it.
Oh, yeah. And the guy's name was Gary something. He was terrific.
But then the show broke up. But Duke was too scary to take the show on his own, because he could have
gotten Mills to back that show up and everybody was willing to play ball, you know, take a chance. But he didn't want to do it.
Well, he talked about it for years. He was very proud of that show.
It was a terrific show.
All those numbers -- Were all of the numbers written for that show?
Yeah.
Because I know some of them became famous later.
Yeah, there were good tunes in there. I mean nice tunes. It would have gone over.
